newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FERDINAND JOINS SHEARER ON INJURED LIST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FERDINAND JOINS SHEARER ON INJURED LIST.

text.p: Newcastle's loss of two points on Saturday will be of less immediate concern than the loss of their second England striker within a month.
Les Ferdinand could be out of action for up to six weeks after suffering a depressed cheekbone fracture during Newcastle's 1-1 draw with West Ham at St James' Park.
It is a crushing blow for manager Kevin Keegan who is already without 15 million pounds ($24.9 million) world record signing Alan Shearer following a groin operation.
Ferdinand was injured challenging for a header inside the West Ham penalty area just before half-time and was led off the pitch looking groggy.

"Les has a depressed cheekbone and we're looking at a month to six weeks," said a despondent Keegan, who will now have to go into Tuesday's UEFA Cup third round first leg tie against Metz in France with a makeshift strike force.

Newcastle were already a goal down when Ferdinand was injured and the fact they managed to salvage a point and stay two points clear at the top of the premier league owed much to veteran Peter Beardsley.

With only eight minutes remaining and Newcastle in danger of their fourth defeat of the season, Beardsley fired home the equaliser, the 200th league goal of his career, to cancel out Keith Rowland's first half opener.
"It's typical of him (Beardsley). He keeps writing the scripts for us," said Keegan.
"Peter came in at half-time and said: I'm having a nightmare'. But I told him: I'll take a nightmare from you because of your enthusiasm', and he goes out in the second half and gets us a goal."
Keegan felt Newcastle were well worth their draw. "It's the least we deserved from the match," he said.
"I'm disappointed we've not got three points but not with the way we've played. There were a lot of pluses, especially the way we stuck at it.
"I said to the players afterwards: "It's like a win when you get a point like that', because it looked as if it was going to be one of those days for us.
"There was plenty of incident and a bit of blood around as well," said Keegan, who also saw Robbie Elliott injured in a clash of heads with Iain Dowie.
"But it wasn't a dirty game. It was a tough game and West Ham stood up for themselves."

Keegan, who has been criticised for the number of goals scored against his team, kept faith with a three-man defence for the game and took the blame for West Ham's goal, left wing-back Rowland heading home a 22nd minute cross from right wing-back Tim Breacker.

"I take full responsibility for the goal because of the system we played," said Keegan. "They got in behind David (Ginola) and Keith (Gillespie) was caught napping by the cross. That's the downside of the way we play."

The system has proved mainly successful because of the goalscoring capacity of twin strikers Shearer and Ferdinand. Whether he can afford to continue with it in the absence of both will cause him some considerable reflection.
